clue.text: Flatten target, then take a nap

parts.note: the bull is the bullseye, the centre of a target
to doze is to have a light sleep

explanation.surface: Instructions for a lazy afternoon: shoot at the target, then sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze a building is to knock it down and level it with heavy machinery.

clue.text: Blemish on skin develops, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: a storm or trouble brews when it develops

explanation.surface: A mark on someone's skin is reported to be getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' says BREWS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A bruise is a dark discoloured patch where skin has been struck.

clue.text: Disorganised, Sally saving time at the end

indicators.note: saving means keeping something inside, so one piece holds the other
disorganised means out of order, so the letters of Sally are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chaotic woman called Sally only puts money aside when it is almost too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorganised' rearranges SALLY into LASLY, and 'saving' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly is used to introduce the final item, meaning finally.

clue.text: Temporarily quiet, party talk loudly about first of members

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to rant is to speak loudly and at length

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word members

explanation.surface: A political party goes briefly silent after a noisy speech about its members.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormant volcano or plant is inactive for now but may wake again.

clue.text: Flies perhaps hurry quicker round gent's middle

parts.note: to zip is to move fast

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: faster means quicker

indicators.note: the middle of the word gent is its central pair of letters

explanation.surface: Insects swarm faster around a man's waist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flies' are the fastening on the front of trousers, not insects; 'perhaps' warns that the definition is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouser flies are often closed with a zip; the 'perhaps' marks it as one example.

clue.text: A rest taken on island? That's the way things are

parts.note: to sit is to rest in a chair

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break on an island and shrugs at how life goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes accepting the present situation unchanged, exactly how matters stand.

clue.text: What's been leaked? Consult attendant

parts.note: to see a doctor is to consult one
a page is a young attendant, as at a wedding or court

explanation.surface: Someone asks what information got out and is told to ask an aide.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid that has slowly escaped through small holes or pores.

clue.text: Love a valuable collection

definitions.meaning: a verb: to cherish or hold dear
a hoard of riches such as gold and jewels

explanation.surface: Someone adores a precious set of objects.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cherish; the noun is a hoard of riches.

clue.text: Position on one's feet

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rank or reputation and being upright rather than seated.

clue.text: Sun playing tricks, loosens ties

indicators.note: letters playing about are moved around, so the word Sun is rearranged

parts.note: traps are tricks or snares to catch someone out

explanation.surface: The sun dazzles and deceives, so someone loosens their necktie in the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Undoing the straps on something releases the bindings that hold it fastened.

clue.text: Groups put in care neglected, looking back

indicators.note: looking back says the hidden letters are read backwards
put in says the answer's letters are placed inside the words care neglected

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Groups of children are taken into care and then neglected, viewed in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Groups put' as the definition, but 'put in' is the signal for the hidden letters ARENEG in 'care neglected'; 'looking back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Genera are biological categories, the ranks grouping related species together.

clue.text: Wife of Ottoman ruler, fruity thing

definitions.meaning: the consort of a Turkish sultan
a dried seedless grape, as used in cakes

explanation.surface: A sultan's consort is described, a little cheekily, as a fruity number.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a sultan's wife and a pale dried grape used in baking.

clue.text: Forced to admit article lauded

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: prised means forced open with a lever
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone was made to confess a newspaper piece they had praised.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud someone is to commend them highly, the same as giving them acclaim.

clue.text: Joker perhaps against wit

parts.note: one team is playing another when it competes against it
a card is a witty, amusing person

explanation.surface: A comedian is pitted against a clever rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joker' looks like a person, but it is the wild card in a pack; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The joker is one card in a standard pack, an example of the category.

clue.text: Bending tree not hard, solid

indicators.note: bending twists the shape, so the letters of tree not hard are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree that is not hard but supple bends rather than staying solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' looks like an instruction to remove H, but all eleven letters of 'tree not hard' are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrahedron is a geometric solid with four triangular faces.

clue.text: Occupying berth, more troubled

indicators.note: occupying means taking up space inside, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a berth is a bed on a ship or train
other can mean additional or more, as in 'other reasons'

explanation.surface: Someone lying in a ship's bunk grows more and more uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bothered means being worried or disturbed.

clue.text: Naked people looking to grab cloak, finally

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: starers are people who stare

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word cloak

explanation.surface: Onlookers seize a cloak to cover someone with no clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' puts K inside STARERS. 'Starkers' is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is informal British slang meaning wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Superior due

definitions.meaning: still unpaid or owing, as a debt

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both excellent and still awaiting payment, two separate senses.

clue.text: Leaders of British union inspired by hackneyed commendation

indicators.note: inspired here means breathed in, so the inner letters go inside the word for hackneyed

parts.note: trite means overused and stale

indicators.note: leaders of takes the opening letters of British and union

explanation.surface: A union boss gives a stale speech of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an act or statement expressing praise or respect.

clue.text: Garnet, I suspect, hard rock

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or not genuine, so the letters of Garnet, I are rearranged

explanation.surface: A geologist doubts a gem and thinks it is really a tough stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard igneous stone used in building.

clue.text: Group of words becomes ragged when spoken

indicators.note: when spoken means judged by its sound in speech

parts.note: fabric that frays becomes ragged at the edges

explanation.surface: A sentence gets garbled when someone says it out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when spoken' says FRAYS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a small set of words forming a unit within a sentence.

clue.text: Five accessing a hollow entrance

indicators.note: accessing means getting into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dent is a hollow made by a blow
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people climb into a cave by its opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival or coming into being, an entrance onto the scene.

clue.text: Hound winger

definitions.meaning: a breed of dog used for hunting hares
something with wings: a bird of prey, or the jump-jet aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a hare-hunting dog breed and to a bird of prey or the British jump jet.

clue.text: Cut around new ground

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: gashed means cut deeply

explanation.surface: Something freshly cut lies around on new earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N inside GASHED. 'ground' looks like a noun but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash teeth is to grind them together, so gnashed is the past form of grinding.

clue.text: Monkey rushes all over the place

indicators.note: scattered in disorder, so the letters of rushes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monkey races around in every direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a species of Asian monkey much used in research.

clue.text: Mark entertains in a talk that's playful

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a badge is a distinguishing mark or emblem

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark amuses a crowd with a light-hearted speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name, but it stands for an emblem worn on clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is witty banter, teasing conversation exchanged in fun.

clue.text: Buttonholed by father, the woman ran

indicators.note: to be buttonholed is to be caught and held, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is cornered for a chat by her father and runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed is the past tense of dash, to hurry or sprint off.

clue.text: Supporter he daren't cast out

indicators.note: cast about or thrown out of order, so the letters of he daren't are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loyal follower whom a man is too afraid to expel.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower who sticks to a cause or leader.
